Heart rate
What were you just doing?
A pulse means nothing on its own. The answer here decides whether this reading counts toward your usual range or is just noted alongside it.
Just woke up
The steadiest reading you can take. Before sitting up, before your phone.
counts
Sitting quietly
Five minutes still, nothing in the last half hour. The everyday reference point.
counts
Just moved
Stairs, a walk, standing up quickly. Logged, but kept out of your usual range.
Had caffeine
Caffeine lifts heart rate for hours. Worth recording, not worth averaging in.
Wound up
Mid-moment. This is the reading the comparison below is actually useful for.
Daylight
I got outside
Say how long, or when
One tap records about 15 minutes, marked as an estimate. It is a log, not a light meter — it cannot tell open noon from overcast dusk, so the time of day is what it weighs.
Tension
Where is it sitting?
Held tension collects in particular places rather than spreading evenly, and it tends to be the same places for the same person. Pick the one you can actually feel — one at a time does more than a list of five.
Jaw, throat and neck
Teeth touching when you notice them. A tight throat, or a headache that starts at the temples.
2m
Chest and front of shoulders
Shoulders that sit forward. A feeling of not being able to get a full breath in.
2m
Between the shoulder blades
An ache between the shoulder blades by the afternoon. Turning to look behind you feels stiff.
3m
Low back
Stiff on standing up after sitting. A dull band across the lower back at the end of the day.
3m
Front of the hips
Tight at the top of the thigh when you stand. A back that feels better walking than sitting.
3m
None of this is medical advice, and none of it can tell you why a number moved. If something feels wrong, ask a professional. In an emergency call 911; for crisis support in the US, call or text 988.
